## New

- **TCP probes for IPv6 targets.** TCP tracing now works for IPv6 addresses as well as IPv4.
- **Columns of your choice.** Right-click a table's header, or open Settings → Columns, to show or hide columns in the hop table and in All targets. **Default widths** there brings back the widths that follow the window after you have dragged a border.
- **PL pcs**: a new column in both tables and in snapshots with the number of lost probes, next to the loss in percent.
- **Hints on the column titles.** The titles are short in every language; hover one to see what the column means.
- **Hop names by reverse DNS can be turned off** (Settings → Tracing → Hop names): Ping Watch then sends no reverse lookups for the routers.

## Changes

- **Hop limit** now only folds the table: the first hop stays, then a row tells how many hops are hidden, then the last ones. Tracing always goes up to 40 hops, so the route and its end are found whatever the limit. Snapshots fold the table the same way.
- **A target that doesn't answer** ends its route one hop past the last router that answered, instead of a long list of silent rows. Its chart keeps its history while the route changes.
- **TCP probes** count a router's "destination unreachable" as a lost probe, as ICMP does. A switched-off server no longer shows up as many rows of one router with good numbers.
- Without administrator rights, a target saved with TCP shows **ICMP\*** in its toolbar, as ICMP stands in for it.
- **Error messages** in the status bar and in the settings are in your language. Windows' own text is kept inside them.
- Links on the About page open the browser with normal rights, also when Ping Watch was restarted as administrator.
- Settings on the Tracing page fit the window again, so switching pages doesn't move it.
- PL% on All targets is colored like in the hop table.
- Labels at the very ends of the time axis are left out, so they don't run into the scale or get cut off.
- Translations: consistent terms in Russian and German, typographic spaces and apostrophes in French, short column titles that fit in German and Spanish.

## Fixes

- **Ping Watch starts on a Windows without the Visual C++ runtime.** Earlier versions stopped at once with "VCRUNTIME140.dll was not found" unless another program had installed that runtime; it is now built into the program.
- **Updating over a running Ping Watch works.** The installer and the uninstaller ask it to quit (as its tray menu's Exit does) and wait for it, also when it runs as administrator; before, they couldn't close it and stopped with a "file in use" error.
- A second Ping Watch started without administrator rights now finds one running as administrator and shows it, instead of starting a second copy over the same database.
- An alert of "no answer" or loss no longer fires at once when the route changes its length (load balancing over paths of different length).
- The history no longer gets a few stray points of the target in the first second of a trace.
- Resetting a target also clears its alert journal when its name has capital letters outside Latin.
- TCP probes stop listening to the network a few seconds after the last TCP trace stops, and don't put the network card in promiscuous mode.
